backend: mixed: cupy for the real scenario measurements (scenario_under_forced_cupy, pytest_after_fix); numpy forced deliberately for the diagnostic reproduction of the ORIGINAL bug (same_scenario_under_forced_numpy_same_seed) -- see the per-section notes.
purpose: Vikunja #203 follow-up: characterize why tests/test_plastic_mask.py::test_plastic_mask_freezes_fixed_synapses failed under certain pytest collection orders, and verify the fix (a hermetic subprocess forcing SIM_BACKEND=cupy).

same_scenario_under_forced_numpy_same_se.note: Reproduces the ORIGINAL failure mode directly: under the numpy backend, this exact tiny seeded network (10 Izhikevich neurons, seed=7) never spikes at all in EITHER config over 500 steps -- fired_any=False both arms -- so the STDP plastic-mask comparison is undefined on this backend for this seed, NOT because the mask goes unenforced.

pytest_repro_before_fix_note: Before the fix (in-process bridge construction, no forced backend), running `pytest tests/test_plastic_mask.py tests/test_enforce_plastic_mask.py` (either file order) reproducibly FAILED test_plastic_mask_freezes_fixed_synapses with 'Plastic weights didn't move (max |dW|=0.000000)' -- because sim/bridge.py resolves its cupy-vs-numpy backend ONCE at first module import in the process (`cp, _backend_name = get_backend()`, sim/bridge.py:44), and test_enforce_plastic_mask.py's own `os.environ.setdefault('SIM_BACKEND','numpy')' (line 30, for its own unrelated determinism purpose) wins that first import whenever both files are collected in one pytest session.

code_read_confirmation.claim: The STDP kernel already applies cp_synapse_plastic_mask UNCONDITIONALLY (sim/bridge.py:10238-10256), matching the documented BDSP/BTSP behavior -- it does not need (and was never gated behind) the Hebbian-only BRAIN_ENFORCE_PLASTIC_MASK flag from merge 509c7137b.
code_read_confirmation.site: sim/bridge.py:10241 (`if self.cp_synapse_plastic_mask is not None:` inside the non-branchless STDP update block)
